sections.title: Executive summary
sections.text: The supported leading explanation is a coupon-related failure coinciding with lower conversion. Its contribution to the decline is not established: the available evidence lacks coupon-attempt outcomes and event-level chronology. A broader checkout issue is a weaker alternative. Treat this diagnosis as provisional.

sections.title: Observed evidence
sections.text:
Sessions, conversion and checkout failures: 4330 sessions and 75 orders over 76 h ending 2026-10-08T00:00:00.000Z (conversion 1.73%); 34 checkout failures (0.79% of sessions). Baseline: conversion 2.36% (-26.5% change), failures per hour +580% change, sessions per hour -2.8% change. Failure codes: coupon_rejected ×34. Simulated storefront records; device and channel slices join orders to their canonical session.

Revenue, orders and conversion versus baseline: Over 76 h ending 2026-10-08T00:00:00.000Z: 75 orders, net revenue £8008.04, 4330 sessions, conversion 1.73%. Baseline (76 h): hourly revenue -28% change, hourly orders -28.6%, hourly sessions -2.8%. Decomposition: sessions share 0.086, conversion share 0.939, AOV share -0.026 of the revenue change. Values are simulated business records; this describes what changed, not why.

sections.text:

checkout failure (weak): Checkout failures overlapped with the conversion decline, so a broader checkout disruption remains possible. The recorded failures are specifically coupon rejections, which weakens the case for a general checkout-path problem.

Compare coupon-attempt sessions with comparable non-attempt sessions, check whether rejection preceded abandonment or completion, and establish event-level timing against the conversion decline. The supplied evidence does not resolve these questions, and the archive limitation prevents fresh checks here.

strategies.downside: Requires evidence not available in this session; no immediate remediation is proposed.

strategies.explanation: Keep operations unchanged while monitoring conversion and coupon failure rate for further evidence. The archived report supports a possible coupon-related issue but does not establish that it caused the decline.
strategies.benefit: Avoids acting on an uncertain diagnosis and preserves the ability to compare subsequent measurements against the current situation.
strategies.downside: If coupon rejection is materially disrupting checkout, monitoring alone may leave the issue unaddressed.
strategies.feasibility: No operational change is required; monitoring depends on metrics becoming available.
strategies.reversibility: No change is made, so there is no operational rollback required.
strategies.uncertainty: The supplied session has no current metric values or fresh source records to establish whether the issue persists.
advisory: Reassess if fresh, scoped evidence becomes available; distinguish coupon-specific failures from broader checkout failures before considering any remediation.
strategies.comparison: This is the least disruptive option, but it will not resolve the stated evidence gaps and may delay response if the issue continues.
